---
title: "Install and run Spinorama"
date: 2026-08-22
abstract: >
  Install the Spinorama development environment, metadata manager, command-line
  tools, and documentation dependencies.
---

This project has two audiences: people who want to run the analysis tools and
people who want to develop or contribute data. The setup script creates the
complete environment. A smaller installation is also provided for users who
only need Python analysis or the metadata manager.

## Requirements

| Tool | Version | Required for |
|---|---|---|
| Python | 3.12 or 3.13 (`>=3.12,<3.14`) | Python tools and metadata manager |
| Git | Any recent version | Source checkout and contributions |
| Node.js/npm | LTS | Website build and JavaScript tests |
| Rust/cargo | Current stable | Optional scoring extension |
| maturin | Current | Optional Rust extension build |
| Quarto | Current | Documentation build |

## Complete setup

### Linux and macOS

Clone the repository and run the setup script from its root:

```{.shell}
git clone https://github.com/pierreaubert/spinorama.git
cd spinorama
./scripts/setup.sh
```

On Linux the script uses `apt` for system packages; on macOS it uses Homebrew.
It creates `.venv`, installs the Python requirement files, installs Node
dependencies, downloads third-party assets, and builds the optional native
extensions when their toolchains are available.

Activate the environment in every new shell:

```{.shell}
source .venv/bin/activate
export PYTHONPATH="$PWD/src:$PWD/src/website${PYTHONPATH:+:$PYTHONPATH}"
```

The `PYTHONPATH` setting is needed because the repository uses a `src` layout
and is normally run from a checkout rather than an installed wheel.

### Windows

Install [Python 3.12](https://www.python.org/downloads/),
[Node.js](https://nodejs.org/), and [Git](https://git-scm.com/), then run:

```powershell
.\scripts\setup.ps1
```

Activate the environment and set the import path in each PowerShell session:

```powershell
.\.venv\Scripts\Activate.ps1
$env:PYTHONPATH = "$PWD\src;$PWD\src\website"
```

The setup script also enables UTF-8 mode for Python on Windows.

## Smaller Python setup

If the system dependencies and the repository's Python environment already
exist, install only the runtime and metadata dependencies:

```{.shell}
python3.12 -m venv .venv
source .venv/bin/activate
python -m pip install -r requirements.txt -r requirements-meta.txt
export PYTHONPATH="$PWD/src:$PWD/src/website"
```

Install the test and development requirements when contributing code:

```{.shell}
python -m pip install -r requirements-test.txt -r requirements-dev.txt
```

## Run the applications

Open the Qt metadata manager with:

```{.shell}
python -m metaedit.app
```

Use `python -m metaedit.app --speaker "Brand Model"` to open an existing
speaker directly. See [Add speaker metadata](03_metadata.qmd) for the complete
workflow and Git/PR requirements.

Compute graphs and preference scores from a directory of measurements with:

```{.shell}
python scripts/compute_spin.py /path/to/measurement-data
```

The command auto-detects supported formats and writes PNG graphs and a
`*_scores.json` file. See [Compute a spinorama](08_compute_spin.qmd) for the
format layout and options.

## Run tests and checks

From the repository root, with the virtual environment active:

```{.shell}
PYTHONPATH=src pytest -q tests
npx vitest
./scripts/check_meta.py
```

Useful formatting and lint checks are:

```{.shell}
ruff format .
ruff check src tests
npx prettier --check src/website
```

Run `./scripts/check_html.sh` when checking generated HTML. The complete
project setup and CI may run additional checks for native extensions and
generated assets.

## Build the documentation

Install Quarto separately, then install the Python packages used by the
documentation examples:

```{.shell}
python -m pip install -r manual/requirements-quarto.txt
quarto render manual
```

The rendered site is written to `dist/docs`. Code examples in the manual are
currently illustrative: execution is disabled in `manual/_quarto.yml`, so
they are not run automatically during rendering.

## Docker

The repository also contains `Dockerfile.base` and `Dockerfile` for a
containerized build:

```{.shell}
docker build -f Dockerfile.base -t spin-base:latest .
docker build -f Dockerfile -t spinorama:latest .
docker run --rm -it spinorama:latest
```

For an interactive shell with the checkout mounted:

```{.shell}
docker run --rm -it -p 5173:5173 -v "$PWD":/work spinorama:latest bash
```

Inside the container, `pytest -q tests` runs Python tests and
`npx vite --host 0.0.0.0 --port 5173` starts the website development server.
